title: Antique Darkroom Shader Laboratory
description: An antique camera sits on a table beside a translucent teacup and a glowing plant. The user manipulates custom post-processing shaders through a multi-step control panel — adjusting chromatic aberration, vignette, film grain, color grading, bloom threshold, and a subsurface-scattering-inspired transmission tint — to compose a perfect vintage photograph captured from the camera's viewpoint.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with es module shims from cdn.jsdelivr.net). Load three GLB assets via GLTFLoader: AntiqueCamera (placed at left, slightly rotated toward center), DiffuseTransmissionPlant (placed behind-center, scaled 2x), and DiffuseTransmissionTeacup (placed on a small surface in front-right of camera). Add a ground plane with a dark wood MeshStandardMaterial. Use a warm-toned PointLight near the plant (simulating bioluminescence) and a dim DirectionalLight from above. Set the main perspective camera behind and slightly above the antique camera, looking at the teacup and plant scene. Implement a custom ShaderPass pipeline using EffectComposer with RenderPass as the base. Build a dat.gui panel (from CDN) with these 8 validated parameters: (1) chromaticAberration (float 0.0–0.02, default 0.0), (2) vignetteIntensity (float 0.0–1.5, default 0.3), (3) vignetteRadius (float 0.1–1.0, default 0.8), (4) filmGrainStrength (float 0.0–0.5, default 0.0), (5) colorTintR/G/B (three floats 0.0–2.0, defaults 1.1, 0.95, 0.8 for sepia warmth), (6) bloomThreshold (float 0.0–1.0, default 0.7), (7) transmissionTint (color hex, default #88ffaa, applied as a uniform that tints fragments where the plant and teacup meshes are rendered using a second render target ID pass). Write a custom fragment shader that samples the scene texture with RGB offset for chromatic aberration, multiplies a vignette falloff, adds time-based film grain noise, applies the RGB color tint, and composites an additive bloom from an UnrealBloomPass. For the transmission tint, render an ID mask of the plant and teacup into a separate RenderTarget, and in the composite shader blend the transmissionTint color where the mask is nonzero. Clamp all GUI inputs to their valid ranges. Add a 'Capture' button that freezes the post-processed frame onto a small preview quad in the bottom-right corner styled as a vintage photo with CSS border. Animate the plant with a gentle vertex-displacement wind sway via onBeforeCompile injection. OrbitControls should be enabled but constrained to a 45-degree arc around the scene.
